title: Equinor’s third quarter 2026 safety results
summary: Equinor's long-term safety trend is stable at the end of the third quarter of 2026.
body_markdown:
At the end of the quarter, the serious incident frequency per million hours worked (SIF) was 0.26, up from 0.25 in the second quarter of 2026. Serious personal injuries are also included in these statistics.


Camilla Salthe, executive vice president for safety, security & sustainability


Photo: Arne Reidar Mortensen / ©Equinor


As of the third quarter, the total recordable injury frequency per million hours worked (TRIF) was 3.1 for the last 12 months, up from 2.8 in the second quarter of 2026.


Nine serious oil and gas leaks were recorded over the last 12 months, up from five in the second quarter of 2026. This includes leaks with a discharge rate above 0.1 kg per second.


"We work on improvements in a systematic and risk-based way, along with our suppliers. Our measures focus on work at heights, the risk of falling objects and occupational injuries," says Camilla Salthe, executive vice president for safety, security & sustainability.


### Preventive work


The focus in the "Always Safe" learning package for the fourth quarter will be health and the working environment.


The goal of this learning package is to prevent hazardous exposure by focusing on issues including increasing understanding of long-term exposure to noise, chemicals and physical strains that are harmful to health.
